AR1.33.notes: The only passage Richter prints from this side (Reference Table: §4 = Br. M. 1a). The Italian here is Richter's printed text, as the brief asks for this class; the Arundel facsimile edition's transcription (1923), which text_source names, was not used. Richter's side heading 'The disorder in the MSS.' is left out. The date is given as Leonardo wrote it.

it.text: Comīciato in Firenze in casa Piero di Braccio Martelli addi 22 di marzo 1508: e questo fia vn racolto sanza ordine, tratto di molte carte le quali io ho qui copiate sperando poi metterle per ordine alli lochi loro, secondo le materie di che esse tratteranno, e credo che auānti ch'io sia al fine di questo, io ci avrò a riplicare vna medesima cosa più volte, si chè lettore nō mi biasimare, perchè le cose son molte e la memoria nō le può riseruare e dire, questa non voglio scriuere perchè dinanzi la scrissi; e se io nō uolessi cadere in tale errore, sarebbe necessario che per ogni caso ch'io uolessi copiare, sicchè per nō replicarlo, io auessi senpre a rilegere tutto il passato, e massime stante co' lunghi interualli di tenpo allo scriuere da una volta a un altra.

en.text: Begun at Florence, in the house of Piero di Braccio Martelli, on the 22nd day of March 1508. And this is to be a collection without order, taken from many papers which I have copied here, hoping to arrange them later each in its place, according to the subjects of which they may treat. But I believe that before I am at the end of this [task] I shall have to repeat the same things several times; for which, O reader! do not blame me, for the subjects are many and memory cannot retain them [all] and say: 'I will not write this because I wrote it before.' And if I wished to avoid falling into this fault, it would be necessary in every case when I wanted to copy [a passage] that, not to repeat myself, I should read over all that had gone before; and all the more since the intervals are long between one time of writing and the next.
en.label: Translation: Jean Paul Richter, 1883

de.text: Begonnen in Florenz, im Haus des Piero di Braccio Martelli, am 22. März 1508. Und dies wird eine Sammlung ohne Ordnung sein, gezogen aus vielen Blättern, die ich hier abgeschrieben habe, in der Hoffnung, sie später an ihren Platz zu ordnen, nach den Gegenständen, die sie behandeln. Und ich glaube, bevor ich hiermit am Ende bin, werde ich ein und dieselbe Sache mehrmals wiederholen müssen. Darum, Leser, tadle mich nicht, denn der Dinge sind viele, und das Gedächtnis kann sie nicht bewahren und sagen: Dies will ich nicht schreiben, weil ich es früher schon geschrieben habe. Und wollte ich nicht in diesen Fehler fallen, so müsste ich bei jedem Stück, das ich abschreiben wollte, um es nicht zu wiederholen, immer das ganze Vorige wieder lesen, zumal bei den langen Zeitabständen zwischen einem Schreiben und dem nächsten.
de.label: Von einer KI aus dem gedruckten Text von Jean Paul Richter, 1883 übersetzt. Sie kann Fehler enthalten.
doubts: 'per ogni caso ch'io uolessi copiare': literally 'for every case I wished to copy'; Richter supplies '[a passage]', we write 'Stück'.

it.text: Questo scriuersi distintamēte del nibbio par che sia mio destino, perchè nella prima ricordatione della mia infantia e' mi parea che, essendo io in culla, che vn nibbio venisse a me e mi aprisse la bocca colla sua coda, e molte volte mi percuotesse cō tal coda dentro alle labra.

en.text: This writing distinctly about the kite seems to be my destiny, because among the first recollections of my infancy, it seemed to me that, as I was in my cradle, a kite came to me and opened my mouth with its tail, and struck me several times with its tail inside my lips.
en.label: Translation: Jean Paul Richter, 1883

de.text: Dass ich so eingehend über den Milan schreibe, scheint mein Schicksal zu sein, denn in der ersten Erinnerung meiner Kindheit kam es mir vor, als ich in der Wiege lag, als ob ein Milan zu mir käme, mir mit seinem Schwanz den Mund öffnete und mich viele Male mit diesem Schwanz innen an die Lippen schlüge.

doubts: 'nibbio' is the kite (German 'Milan'), not a vulture.
'Questo scriuersi distintamēte del nibbio': literally 'this writing oneself so distinctly about the kite'; we write 'Dass ich so eingehend über den Milan schreibe'.

AR3.181.notes: Placement confirmed (facts-0929 Q1): Richter prints 'Br. M. 272a]' (British Museum, Arundel 263, fol. 272 recto), his Bibliography (vol. II p. 492) lists '272a 1372', and the Reale Commissione Vinciana edition of 1923 prints it under 'Fol. 272 recto', p. 438. Richter's footnote begins: 'This statement of Ser Piero's age contradicts that of the Riassunto della portata di Antonio da Vinci (Leonardo's grandfather), who speaks of Ser Piero as being thirty years old in 1457; and that of the Riassunto della portata di Ser Piero e Francesco, sons of Antonia da Vinci, where Ser Piero is mentioned as being forty in 1469. These documents were published by G. Uzielli, Ricerche intorno a L. da Vinci, Firenze, 1872, pp. 144 and 146.' Any displayed caption should not present the age 80 as fact. A second note of the same death, on another sheet, is Richter's §1373, from a sheet of the Codex Atlanticus; it is not on this page. The curator's reason points to this passage: lead 0.

it.text: A dì 9 di luglio 1504, mercoledì a ore 7 morì Ser Piero da Vinci, notaio al Palazzo del Podestà, mio padre, a ore 7, era d'età d'anni 80, lasciò 10 figlioli maschi e 2 femmine.

en.text: On the 9th of July 1504, Wednesday, at seven o'clock, died Ser Piero da Vinci, notary at the Palazzo del Podestà, my father,—at seven o'clock, being eighty years old, leaving behind ten sons and two daughters.
en.label: Translation: Jean Paul Richter, 1883

de.text: Am 9. Juli 1504, Mittwoch, zur 7. Stunde starb Ser Piero da Vinci, Notar am Palazzo del Podestà, mein Vater, zur 7. Stunde. Er war 80 Jahre alt und hinterließ 10 Söhne und 2 Töchter.
de.label: Von einer KI aus dem gedruckten Text von Jean Paul Richter, 1883 übersetzt. Sie kann Fehler enthalten.
doubts: 'a ore 7': literally 'at hour 7'; kept literal ('zur 7. Stunde'). Richter: 'at seven o'clock'.
Leonardo repeats the hour ('a ore 7' twice); the repetition is kept.
'era d'età d'anni 80' is Leonardo's statement; Richter's footnote says it contradicts the family tax returns (see notes). The translation keeps Leonardo's number.

doubts: 'ganbe' means legs; Richter's English prints 'eyes'. The German follows the Italian.
'coppi': vessels, jars or roof tiles; Richter reads 'pitchers' with a question mark. We write 'Gefäße' and mark it.
'gruppi': knots, interlaced patterns; Richter's footnote links them to the knot designs Vasari describes.
'zīgana': we keep the historical word as 'Zigeunerin', as Richter keeps 'gypsy girl'; the museum may want to gloss it.
'gole di vechie': throats or necks of old women; Richter reads 'throats'.
'fatta in forma': made in a mould; Richter reads 'a cast'.
'Atalāta che alzava il uolto': the tense is past ('was raising'); the German uses the present, as a picture title would.

L.007.notes: Placement confirmed (facts-0929 Q1 and Ravaisson): all three passages carry 'L. o']' (Richter's key: o' is inside the front cover); his Bibliography (vol. II p. 490, L) lists 'o' 1414, 1323, 1102'; Ravaisson vol. V prints all three under 'Ms L, 1er VERSO DE LA COUVERTURE' with footnotes to Richter nos. 1414, 1323 and 1102 (the Rhodes line is written in the margin) (https://archive.org/details/lesmanuscritsdel05lo/page/n207/mode/1up). Given in the edition's order (§1102, §1323, §1414); on the cover the pen and penknife note stands among the lines of §1414. Richter's footnote to §1414: '4-10. This passage evidently refers to events in Milan at the time of the overthrow of Ludovico il Moro. Amoretti published it in the Memorie Storiche and added copious notes.' His notes 6 and 8 quote Amoretti in Italian on the Visconti and on Borgonzio Botta. Ravaisson's note: 'Note en souvenir des événements qui accompagnèrent la chute du duc de Milan, Ludovic le More, en 1499-1500.' The cover also carries sums (3, 100, 77; 72, 2, 144; 5500, 7500, 13000) that Richter does not print. The curator's reason points to the note on the fall of Ludovico il Moro: lead 2.

de.text:
Paolo di Vannoccio in Siena.
Der kleine Saal oben für die Apostel.
Bauten von Bramante.
Der Kastellan gefangen genommen.
Der Visconti fortgeschleift, und danach sein Sohn tot.
Gian della Rosa, dem man sein Geld genommen hat.
Borgonzo fing an und wollte es nicht, und darum entging ihm das Glück [?].
Der Herzog hat seinen Staat, seine Habe und seine Freiheit verloren, und keines seiner Werke wurde von ihm vollendet.
de.label: Von einer KI aus dem gedruckten Text von Jean Paul Richter, 1883 übersetzt. Sie kann Fehler enthalten.
doubts: The German reads 'libertà' (Freiheit): Richter's 1883 page prints 'li-' / 'ertà' across a line break, the b missing (checked in a second copy, archive.org literaryworksofl02leon, which has the same misprint); his own variant note reads 'elliberta' and Ravaisson prints 'elliberta'.
Richter's semicolons are turned into full stops; the notes are a list, one item per line as he prints them.
'Il Visconte': Richter reads a member of the Visconti family (his footnote quotes Amoretti: which Visconti is not known); it could also be read as 'the viscount'. Kept as 'der Visconti'.
'e poi morto il figliuolo': 'morto' can mean dead or killed; Richter: 'his son killed'. Kept open as 'tot'.

'Borgonzo principiò e nol volle, e però fuggì le fortune': the sense is unclear, marked [?]. Richter leaves a gap ('Borgonzio began . . . .; and moreover his fortunes fled'); Ravaisson: 'Borgonzo commença et ne le voulut plus, et pour cela ses chances lui échappèrent'. Richter's footnote (after Amoretti): Borgonzio Botta was in charge of the duke's revenues under il Moro, and his house was sacked by the French party after il Moro fled.
'nessuna sua opera si finì per lui': 'per lui' can mean 'by him' or 'for him'; read as 'by him', with Richter ('none of his entreprises was carried out by him').

it.text:
Delle taccole e stornelli.

Quelli che si fideranno abitare appresso di lui, che sarāno grā turbe, questi tutti morirāno di crudele morte, e si vedrā i padri e le madri d'insieme colle sue famiglie esser da crudeli animali divorati e morti.

en.text:
Of tricks [or of magpies] and of burlesque poems [or of starlings].

Those who trust themselves to live near him, and who will be a large crowd, these shall all die cruel deaths; and fathers and mothers together with their families will be devoured and killed by cruel creatures.
en.label: Translation: Jean Paul Richter, 1883

de.text:
Elstern und Stare

Wer sich getrauen wird, neben ihnen zu wohnen, — es werden große Schwärme sein, — fast alle werden eines grausamen Todes sterben, und man wird die Väter, die Mütter und zugleich deren Familien von grausamen Tieren verzehrt und getötet sehen.
de.label: Übersetzung: Marie Herzfeld, 1906
